subject: Request: Hosted API unit pricing (input/output) & supported models
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@cobalthealth.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask: unit IO pricing + models

Hi Soojin,

We're mapping out the economics for a Q1 pilot and need a quick baseline: what are Redwood's standard per-1M token rates split by input vs output for the hosted API? Also, can you send the list of models you certify for production (and any notes on recommended default for latency-sensitive use cases)?

We're primarily interested in 10M tokens/month as a reference and an estimate for an expected 60/40 input/output split. Procurement will need a high-level ratecard and an SLA summary.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Integrations, CobaltHealth
alex@cobalthealth.ai
+1 (415) 555-0197

--
Attachment: none
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@cobalthealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask: unit IO pricing + models

Hi Alex — great to hear from you. Thanks for the context.

Short answer (baseline hosted API rates, per 1M tokens):
- Input tokens: $8.00 per 1M tokens
- Output tokens: $24.00 per 1M tokens

Notes: these are our standard list rates for hosted models without committed volume. Embeddings and specialized vision models are priced separately.

Certified model roster (production-ready on hosted API):
- redwood-1.0 (default low-latency; good for chat/short-turn interactions)
- redwood-2.7b-quant (balanced cost/latency for throughput-sensitive workloads)
- llama-3b-redwood (higher-quality, moderate latency)
- llama-7b-mt (best for longer-context tasks; higher token cost)

Recommendation: for latency-sensitive interactions with short turns we suggest starting on redwood-1.0; if you need higher quality completions and can accept slightly higher latency, try llama-3b-redwood.

I've attached a short baseline ratecard and our standard MAT SLA summary for procurement: redwood_baseline_ratecard_q4_2026.pdf, redwood_standard_sla_mat.pdf.

Ballpark cost example (60/40 IO split, hosted list rates):
- 10M tokens total/month => 6M input + 4M output
- Input cost: 6 * $8.00 = $48.00
- Output cost: 4 * $24.00 = $96.00
- Estimated monthly token cost: $144.00 (list prices)

If you'll be committing to 3–12 month reserved spend, we can explore volume discounts and a dedicated throughput path. Can you confirm expected monthly peak QPS and whether you need regional residency (US/EU)? Also, what latency SLOs are you targeting? That will help us recommend a model/commit tier.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you'd like to review options.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_baseline_ratecard_q4_2026.pdf (summary), redwood_standard_sla_mat.pdf
From: Alex Moreno <alex@cobalthealth.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask: unit IO pricing + models

Thanks Soojin,

Helpful — and impressively concise. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and engineering:
1) Is that $8/$24 gross list or does it already assume the common 50/50 IO split many vendors publish? You confirmed the 60/40 split above but procurement wants the per-side numbers.
2) For our pilot estimate, procurement is asking what discount bands look like for committed monthly volumes (e.g., 10M, 50M, 200M). Any standard % ranges you can share?
3) We operate across US + EU — is the certified model roster identical for EU-hosted instances? Any model residency caveats we should surface to legal?

Lastly, procurement wants a one-page PDF with those 3 example monthly cost lines (10M/50M/200M) at list and at a conservative discount band so they can include it in initial budget planning. Can you provide that?

Appreciate it — Alex

Alex — quick follow-up with the conservative discount bands and answers to your questions.

1) The $8/$24 are gross list prices per 1M tokens (no implicit IO normalization). When teams quote a blended rate some vendors publish an average; we keep input/output separated so you can model your ratio.

2) Typical discount tiers (hosted API, customer examples):
- 10M token/month: 5% off list as an introductory committed plan
- 50M token/month: 12% off list on a 6–12 month commit
- 200M+ token/month: 20%+ off list with enterprise contract & SLA

These are conservative starting points — exact discounts depend on term length, prepayment, and whether you need dedicated capacity. We can provide a formal quote after you confirm expected monthly volume and term.

3) Certified models: roster is identical between US and EU regions for our hosted API. If you choose private deployment or on-prem, there are additional residency/legal requirements; we'd flag that separately.

Attached is a one-pager with 10M/50M/200M examples at list and at the conservative discount tier (see redwood_baseline_ratecard_q4_2026.pdf). Procurement and legal can use the MAT SLA (redwood_standard_sla_mat.pdf) as the starting doc for security/residency questions.

Next steps suggestion:
- If the ballpark looks reasonable, I can arrange a 30-minute call with Ben (pricing lead) to model your expected monthly mix and produce a formal quote.

Would Tuesday morning PST work for a quick call?

— Soojin
